summary.text: Amanda McKinney is a Republican and a member of the Yakima County Board of Commissioners, first elected in 2020, who is running for the open 4th District seat after Rep. Dan Newhouse announced he would not seek reelection. She describes herself as an America First Republican whose priorities include defending faith, family, agriculture, and rural Washington. She led the August 4 top-two primary with 34.9%.

paragraphs.text: Was first elected to the Yakima County Board of Commissioners in 2020 and currently serves on it.

As commissioner, has focused on water and agriculture, including support for the Yakima Basin Integrated Plan, a county water bank built through senior water rights acquisition, and floodplain restoration projects; the Yakima Herald also reports she opposed prolonged COVID-19 shutdowns and vaccine mandates and has supported law enforcement, emergency communications, and efforts to address fentanyl and violent crime.
In 2024 she appeared in a television ad supporting Rep. Dan Newhouse's reelection against Jerrod Sessler, a Trump-endorsed Republican challenger.

Announced her congressional campaign days after Newhouse said he would not seek reelection; the seat is open for the first time in about a decade. Her seat on the county commission (Position 1) drew other candidates' filings for 2026.

Describes herself as an America First Republican aligned with President Trump on border security, the Second Amendment, and eliminating DEI programs. Trump endorsed her campaign on January 6, 2026, as did House Speaker Mike Johnson.
